response.reason: The binary search maintains the invariant count(x >= lo) >= k, and the final keep mask (x >= lo) guarantees every kept entry is at least the converged threshold while every dropped entry is below it, so the contract's ordering requirement holds (ties at the cutoff are all admitted, which is an accepted reading). Only degenerate cases like k=0 (which would keep ties at the maximum) are arguably mishandled, but that's outside typical top-k sampling usage.
